headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: dexter can emit sensitive financial context while slim can read/write files and execute shell commands, creating leakage and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ and uses autonomous execution, while slim reads/writes filesystem artifacts and processes stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if dexter output is placed where slim parses it. No shared clipboard or MCP is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF dexter output is copied into a file or stdin stream that slim parses as commands or config
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace without content provenance checks
mitigations: Keep dexter and slim in separate directories
Disable automatic parsing of dexter-generated text by slim
Require a human review step before any slim command execution
Use read-only mounts for dexter outputs where possible
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API calls, while slim reads filesystem artifacts and handles registry credentials and private keys. If they share a workspace, dexter can expose sensitive files to its APIs and slim can ingest them, creating a realistic exfiltration path with broad blast radius.
conditions: IF dexter and slim share a filesystem or mounted workspace
IF sensitive files from slim's target image are present in dexter-readable paths
IF dexter forwards those contents through its external APIs
mitigations: Separate workspaces and mount points
Remove secrets from any shared directory before running either agent
Block dexter from sending file contents to external APIs
Run slim on sanitized copies of images and artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dexter supports multiple instances and autonomous execution, while slim can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. They do not both advertise unrestricted writes to the same directory, so the strongest conflict case is not proven; however, overlapping write-adjacent authority still creates contention risk in shared targets.
conditions: IF both agents are launched against the same mutable workspace
IF dexter-generated artifacts are edited by slim during the same run
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Serialize access to shared artifacts
Avoid concurrent runs on the same target image
Use file locks for any shared outputs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter's autonomous execution can generate analysis or actions that slim may consume through stdin/stdout or files, and slim can then execute shell commands based on that input. Because slim has action-taking authority, a mistaken dexter output can cascade into irreversible container changes or destructive commands without a verification gate.
conditions: IF slim treats dexter output as authoritative input
IF slim executes commands derived from dexter-produced text without human verification
mitigations: Insert a manual approval step before slim executes commands
Require schema validation on dexter outputs
Log and diff all commands before execution
Restrict slim to dry-run mode where possible
requires-engineering: add output attestation and verification

E_compliance.rationale: dexter handles financial data and market data, while slim handles filesystem artifacts, environment variables, certificate private keys, and registry credentials. If the same regulated or secret-bearing data is processed by both, differing retention and residency obligations can be violated; the profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is present in slim's target artifacts
IF either agent retains logs or artifacts beyond the required retention window
IF secrets or private keys are copied into dexter's external API calls
mitigations: Minimize retention of logs and artifacts
Exclude secrets and private keys from shared inputs
Confirm data residency requirements before processing
Use redacted copies for analysis
requires-engineering: document and enforce compliance boundaries
